about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.
plan: Shared by all six shots and recorded in README.md's capture block: window 1440x763 on the deployed build at ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.boot(); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30), then DEV.cam(...) and one DEV.tick(1) per shot, vitals pinned at 100, the level's own hostiles cleared (never DEV.clear()), level banner taken down with banner('', 0). A frozen clock does not stop S.t, so these frames are reproducible by statistics and never by md5. **One term this plan did not record: the audio device.** A live boot advances the seeded stream through SND.init's noise buffer before the generator runs, so one seed deals one level per sample rate (#404, and the rule the tool prints as HW_WHY). These six captures read no SND.ac.sampleRate, so every row carries `sampleRate: null`, `check` prints each one as a device-scoped deal, and the binding below is per-machine: it says this frame is what ?dev=1&seed=60 dealt on the capture's audio device, not that every machine deals it. `STRICT=1 node tools/recap.js check` gates the missing term. A capture that reads the rate turns its own row into a cross-machine binding with no change to the tool.

shots.note: Deal transcribed from README.md's capture block, which names all six shots as one route: the deployed page opened at ?dev=1&seed=60, build proved by eval-visible code markers, every deployed js blob md5-identical to the tree at ce9d39d. layout is that block's DEV.layoutSig() for the deal. Pose: one posed grunt 6 m out on the camera's own band (a posed body added with DEV.spawn, never DEV.clear, which would leave 0 LEFT on the HUD).

Same route as level0-spawn; see that row for where each field was recorded. Shot 8be1f96 is the one whose caption names black air above the four risers - the reason #333 reopened, and the reason this artifact exists.
Same route as level0-spawn. Feet on floor -1.00 in the pit, lamp at (20.5, 16.5) one cell over - a pose named in the caption, so the deal field is what makes it re-takeable rather than a description.
Same route as level0-spawn. The pit lip from 2.5 m out; the props the caption counts (9 lamps, 7 crates, 7 barrels) are this deal's, which is why seed and layout are gated and the counts are not.

The reference shot for the block: the route and every deal field in these six rows are transcribed from README.md's capture block (deployed build, ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.layoutSig 735688443, js blobs md5-identical to ce9d39d) rather than re-measured here. #335 measured this route: reloading the same URL read DEV.seed 60 and layout 735688443 on both loads, which is what makes origin+install=url-open a binding route.

Re-taken at ed5faf4 (#388, sixth frame for this seat) because #407 - a body or a prop keeps the lamp field of the cell it stands in instead of paying exp(-d x 0.14) of it - landed on main while the previous take of this row was in review. This row is addressed to the build the pixels were DRAWN at, which is a fact of the capture and not of any tree that later merges it: the page that served this shutter ran index.html 44b7f0ca over js/40_render.js 7942de4b, js/90_dev.js c36909c9, js/00_core.js ac12ee35, js/13_mesh.js f222d5ec, js/20_level.js 9b24d5c4 and js/10_assets.js 3f00716c. The row deliberately does NOT claim the merged tree's js/ blobs equal these - a docs-only PR ships whatever main's renderer is at merge time, so that claim is false the moment any js/ file lands, and it has cost this row three takes. What is claimed instead is measured on both trees: this branch merges main at b85a671, whose only js/ difference from ed5faf4 is js/20_level.js 9b24d5c4 -> deb7e867, #353's overlook pairing pass (index.html and the other ten blobs identical on both sides), and that pass cannot reach an authored seat - LEVELS[3].authored is true, so genLevel returns at the buildAuthored branch before the pairing pass and before authorOverlooked, and overlookPairs is filled only inside authorVolume. The measurement agrees: SEAT=1.5,2.5,0.6 node tools/view.js scene 3 prints framebuffer md5 340f2e85989a19ea34a908dab8eefb05 at mean 49.5 with this branch's js/, with main's js/, and again on a second untouched run, and FP_DEALT=1 FP_DEALT1=3 node tools/view.js flatparity prints dealt level 3 4b644b164e5b63b09fc69d5fc3256971 mean 37.2 off-datum 134/256 on both trees - the value tools/refs.lock carries at main. So these bytes are still the frame the shipping build draws at this seat, and this take re-labelled rather than re-rendered; turning that sentence into a gate is #395. Route is unchanged and is the URL itself: headless Chromium opened this row's url at a 1440x763 device-metrics override at scale 1 and, once the page reported ready, ran DEV.boot(); startLevel(3, true); banner('', 0); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30); P.hp = 100; DEV.cam(1.5, 2.5, floorAt(1.5, 2.5), 0.60, 0); DEV.tick(1), leaving the level's own 4 hostiles standing. The blur rule the previous row recorded still holds - a page that never acquires a pointer lock pauses on the first blur and the overlay dims everything under it, so the route ends with the game's own resume() plus one DEV.tick(1) and re-reads S.mode immediately before the shutter, which is also why the route runs after ready rather than from a document-time script; S.mode read 'play' at both probes on all three runs. THREE runs of that route at this head ALL read DEV.layoutSig() 2733654509, the value this row has always carried - the two untouched ones and the bodydist A/B - so this frame's deal reproduced at this build. It did not at the build before it: the same route there read 3233039185 twice and, issued several seconds after ready, 1900969947, and startLevel(3, true) called twice inside one already-open page read 1730990788 then 1523817166. startLevel generates from wherever the seeded stream has reached and generation advances it, so the deal a run lands on is a property of the run and of the build that ran it, not of the url - pinning the stream before startLevel (#420) is still the only way to make a stored frame re-takeable and a deal number re-readable. DEV.state().gnd reads fade 1 beside jit 1, light 1, ax 1, filt 1, ramp 1, far 1, jitMinPx 48, axMin 1.5, mipax 1, mipar 4, and DECOR reads 14 with FIX_DEP {DOOR 0.12, PIPE 0.10, STRIPE 0.03, VENT 0.08} as before, so #19's blend and #400's stood-off fixture are both still terms of these pixels - but neither is what moved this frame. DEV.state() prints no bodydist key, so #407's term was read as the BODYDIST global, which reads 1 on this page, and DEV.set('bodydist', 0) is its A/B switch. props 9, lights 7, sr 44100, buf 678x359 upscaled to a 1440x763 canvas. Against the bytes this row replaces (5a459714, drawn at fc7a555): mean 50.50 -> 50.60, thirds 41.82 / 58.88 / 50.83 -> 41.82 / 59.19 / 50.82, channels 49.6 / 51.1 / 47.7 -> 49.8 / 51.1 / 47.7, 0 rows below luma 24 in both. 11,712 of 1,098,720 px move by more than 2 luma (1,648 / 8,947 / 1,117 by thirds), worst 73.2, mean |delta| over those px 10.89; 233 px move by more than 50 and every one of them sits inside x 644-1392 x y 328-390 - the standing things at the foot of the TECH wall. By row band the move is rows 317-444, 7,069 px there against the 2,552 those same bands account for in route noise, and the one place it lands on geometry rather than on a body is rows 300-330, 38.2 there and 38.8 here. Everything that does not stand still is unchanged: the x 660-1295 x y 340-422 band 83.2 in both, rows 140-180 44.7 in both, the lit floor at rows 400-600 64.6 in both, and the row-mean thirds move 0.00 / -0.31 / 0.00. The term was measured in the live page rather than argued: the same route at the same build with DEV.set('bodydist', 0) applied before the shutter comes back to 6,516 px over 2 luma, worst 6.0, mean |delta| 2.42 and at most 0.01 in any row-mean third, against 6,925 px worst 6.0 for two runs of the route with no switch touched. So #407 is the whole move and what is left is this route's own noise floor; the deal did not move (layout 2733654509 on all three runs), which is what a renderer term looks like in a caption that has been reading deal moves. Two runs at one build are not byte-identical even so - they differ in 6,925 px by up to 6 in one channel - so this sha256 names THIS capture, not every run of the route. SND.ac.sampleRate read 44100, so this row is a cross-machine binding where the other five are device-scoped.
